ctoi_purpose_and_criteria:
Bottom line: since 19 Aug 2026, ExoFOP only accepts community candidates (CTOIs) that have already been published in a peer-reviewed journal, and the uploader must first be approved. None of our results has been published, so none of them can be uploaded as a CTOI right now.

Current rules (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/candidate_help.php, also on help.php; fetched 2026-10-12):
- Definition: "Community TESS Objects of Interest (cTOIs) are intended to be a mechanism for community members to identify planetary systems or other potentially interesting objects discovered by TESS but not identified as a TESS Object of Interest (TOI) by the TESS project."
- Publication: "Candidates must be published in a peer-reviewed journal that offers online access before being uploaded to ExoFOP." Also: "ExoFOP will only allow upload of Community Candidates accepted and published in the refereed literature. The URL link to the paper must be provided."
- Research Notes exception: "Candidates can also be presented in a Research Note of the American Astronomical Society (RNAAS) if the methodology to detect and vet the candidate has been previously published in a peer-reviewed journal that is available online and is cited by the Research Note."
- Quality: "Insufficiently or ill-defined candidates are not a useful product for the community... poorly defined or duplicate candidates will be removed and may result in suspension or removal of your account."
- Parameters: at least 2 of period, epoch (BJD) and depth (ppm), each > 0. "For cTOI (TESS data source) consideration by the TESS Object of Interest working group, all four of orbital period, transit epoch, transit depth, and transit duration must be included."
- Duplicates: you must cross-check against existing candidates, TOIs and confirmed planets. If the period equals (or is an integer multiple of) a known one, add a parameter set to that object instead of creating a new one.
- Supporting files: material such as a light-curve plot must be uploaded to the TIC host star under the same data tag. "Without supporting material, candidates may be removed."

Timeline (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/news.php):
- 31 Mar 2026: "ExoFOP has temporarily paused the functionality for users to upload new planet candidates (CTOIs and other projects)."
- 19 Aug 2026: "ExoFOP has reopened support... going forward candidates must first be published in a peer-reviewed journal with online access before being uploaded to ExoFOP, and approval to upload candidates is required."

Older descriptions:
- Guerrero et al. 2021 (ApJS 254, 39, §8.4; arXiv:2103.12538): CTOIs are "objects of interest identified by pipelines in the community and reported on ExoFOP-TESS... ExoFOP emphasizes CTOIs should only be reported if there is no TOI with the same period. The TOI team periodically checks for matches on TIC ID and period between the CTOI list... and the... TCEs." All CTOIs promoted to TOIs "were also TCEs in the SPOC pipeline or the QLP."
- Christiansen et al. 2025 (arXiv:2506.03299): CTOIs need "a required minimal set of parameters that allows the TESS Science Office to search for the signal and, if appropriate, promote the signal to a TOI."
- The TESS FAQ (https://tess.mit.edu/?p=1262) still says "If you find a planet candidate submit it to ExoFOP-TESS. Your candidate will become a community TOI (cTOI)". In practice the August 2026 ExoFOP rule now overrides this.

Uptake since reopening, from today's ctoi.csv: every CTOI touched after 2026-03-31 that carries a Paper URL is published work. lafargamagro uploaded 1,173 RAVEN candidates on 2026-08-27 citing Lafarga et al. 2026, MNRAS. mason uploaded one PHT candidate on 2026-10-08 citing an RNAAS paper (doi 10.3847/2515-5172/aeaee1).
ctoi_dispositions_allowed:
There is no "EB" disposition. An eclipsing binary goes in as FP, with the reason in the note.
- New candidates (candidate_help.php): the initial disposition is optional and may be FP (false positive) or PC (planet candidate). CP is not allowed for new candidates.
- Bulk template (templates/params_planet_YYYYMMDD_001.txt): for newctoi the values are blank, FP or PC. For newparams they are blank, CP (confirmed planets only), FP or PC.
- Notes are required for a new CTOI and limited to 120 characters. A paper URL is required for flag=newctoi.

Observed in today's ctoi.csv (5,138 rows), User Disposition: PC 5,088, FP 16, CP 1, blank 33.
fp_or_eb_ctoi_practice:
Short answer: an FP/EB CTOI is permitted but not encouraged, it is rare, and today it would need a published paper.
- No ExoFOP, TESS or Guerrero+2021 text found that encourages filing a known false positive "to save follow-up effort".
- The rules do allow FP as an initial disposition, and the cTOI definition includes "other potentially interesting objects". So FP CTOIs are allowed.
- But they make up 0.3% of all CTOIs (16 of 5,138), none came from a published paper, and none has been filed since the August 2026 reopening.

The 16 FP CTOIs in ctoi.csv (user, CTOI lastmod, note):
- earley: 24725031.01 (2019-09, "Eclipsing binary candidate in Pisces-Eridanus stellar stream") and 360205899.01 (2019-09, EB candidate in the Carina young moving group).
- montet: 116887189.01 (2020-02, RV binary from Brown+2020 that TESS shows to be eclipsing) and 148158540.01 (2019-12, "Eccentric EB with clear primary and secondary", UCL association).
- palumbo: 284910127.01 (2020-08, "Eclipsing Binary").
- deen: 27858644.01 (2021-03, "FP: Contaminated transit from nearby EB"; no period, depth 67,000 ppm). This is the closest precedent to our TIC 87055304 case.
- lynch: 185336364.01 (2022-12), 100029948.03 (2025-09, "Eclipsing Binary Candidate") and 390855216.01 (2025-09, "Eclipsing Binary Candidate (Heart and Soul Nebulae)").
- bryant (group tfopwg): 60910638.01, 311555090.01 and 406717909.01 (2025-02). These are candidates from Bryant et al. 2023 (MNRAS) that ESPRESSO or HPF data show to be SEB/FP.
- devadas: 300651846.01 (2026-02, "Rejected as a Background Eclipsing Binary... 50.7 arcsecond centroid offset").
- ghall: 308794367.01 (2026-03, no note).
- takahashi: 434937879.01 (2026-03, "Candidate eclipsing binary (EB) identified via Planet Hunters TESS").
- cao: 805805533.01 (2026-03, "Likely EB (Deep Signal)").
- The only CP is osborn's 449566969.01 (tfopwg, 2026-02).

What happened to them:
- None of the 16 FP CTOIs was promoted to a TOI ("Promoted to TOI" is empty for all).
- None of their TIC IDs appears in toi.csv, and none has a TFOPWG disposition.
- None has an entry in the Paper column. Only 1,174 CTOIs have one, all from lafargamagro or mason.
- All 16 predate the 31 Mar 2026 pause. The four from 2026 (devadas, ghall, takahashi, cao) are unpublished and would not be accepted under today's rules.
- For comparison, 814 of 5,138 CTOIs overall have been promoted to TOIs.

Our interpretation: under current policy, an FP CTOI for TIC 87055304 (or TIC 87055315) would need a peer-reviewed paper, or an RNAAS that cites peer-reviewed detection and vetting methods, plus approval to upload. Guerrero+2021 says the TOI team cross-matches CTOIs against TCEs by TIC ID and period. So a published FP CTOI could warn TOI vetters if QLP ever produces a TCE for it. The ExoFOP pages do not document that benefit.
who_can_submit_and_how:
Submitting takes three separate approvals.

1) An ExoFOP account (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/account.php).
- Requirement: "You need to be conducting astronomical observational, modelling, or theoretical work at a level consistent with publication in a professional journal and relevant to follow-up studies of exoplanet candidates. Please include the name of the university, research center or similar facility with which you are affiliated."
- Required fields: first and last name, Affiliation, Position and email. Position options are Faculty/staff, Postdoc, Grad student, Undergrad, Citizen Scientist and Other.
- "Registration is not instantaneous"; staff email a username once the request is approved. Requesting an account means agreeing to the Professional Conduct Policy.
- That policy (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/pcp.php) says "Users are professional astronomers or other persons with demonstrated interest in, and capabilities relevant to, the Kepler, K2, or TESS missions" and that NExScI may delete accounts in cases of abuse.

2) Permission to upload candidates: "To request access to submit published candidates, complete the Published Candidate Upload Request. After approval, then you can submit candidates."
- The form is at https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/pub_candidate_upload_request.php and shows "You must be logged in to view this page."
- Its content and the approval criteria were not visible, so not verified.

3) The upload itself, either through the web form on the target page ("Add new Community Planet Candidates or Planet Parameters") or by bulk upload (add_new.php?param=bulkparams).
- Bulk file name: params_planet_YYYYMMDD_nnn.txt, pipe-delimited.
- Columns: target|flag|disp|discovery|candname|period|period_unc|epoch|epoch_unc|depth|depth_unc|duration|duration_unc|inc|...|vsa|vsa_unc|tag|group|prop_period|paper|notes
- target is TICnnn.nn and flag is newctoi. epoch must be BJD > 2,000,000. A data tag (format YYYYMMDD_username_description_nnn) is required. prop_period must be 0 for new CTOIs. The paper URL is required. Notes are required, 120 characters at most.
- Also required: at least 2 of period, epoch and depth, all four (including duration) for TOI-team consideration, the next free TIC.nn name, and a discovery source (blank or "TESS" for TESS data).
- Supporting files must go on the TIC host page under the same tag. Questions go to exofop-support@ipac.caltech.edu "prior to uploading data".

Rules on automated or AI-generated submissions:
- None found on candidate_help.php, help.php, pcp.php, account.php or news.php. The only gates are publication, the two approvals and staff review ("poorly defined or duplicate candidates will be removed and may result in suspension or removal of your account").
- If the RNAAS route is used, the AAS "Author Guidelines for Use of AI and LLMs in Manuscript Preparation" apply (https://journals.aas.org/author-llm-guidelines/; page text: "initially posted on 9 September 2026"). From WebFetch extraction of that page:
  - "AI cannot be listed as an author"
  - authors "must disclose" LLM use, naming the tool and what it was used for
  - "LLMs may not be used to generate any portion of a manuscript unsupervised"
  - violations may be treated as "fraudulent misrepresentation", with retraction or bans possible.
  - The page applies to "AAS journals". That it covers RNAAS is our assumption; it is not stated explicitly in what we extracted.
other_exofop_channels:
These channels are separate from candidate uploads. All of them need a logged-in ExoFOP account and a data tag (help.php, "Uploading Data to ExoFOP": "You must have an account and be logged in to enter or update data").

Available upload types (help.php; bulk_upload_files_inst.php):
- Files on target pages. Codes: F finding chart, I image, L light curve, P photometry, S spectrum, O other. Bulk naming: TICxxxC-xxDATESTAMP[info].ext, plus a pipe-delimited descriptor (filename|tag|group|prop months|description) inside a zip or tar named xxYYYYMMDD-nnn.
- Observing notes. Bulk template obsnotes-YYYYMMDD-nnn.txt with columns Target|Tag|Group|Prop period|Filename. The target can be any TIC ID, not only TOIs.
- Observation summaries (Imaging, Spectroscopy, Time Series tables). These are always public immediately.
- Stellar parameters, stellar companions, and planet parameters. Planet parameters can only be attached to existing TOIs, CTOIs or confirmed planets.

Who can use them:
- Any approved account holder (account rules as in the previous section). No separate approval is documented for notes or files, unlike candidates. We could not log in to confirm; the bulk observing-notes page returns "Sorry, you are not authorized to view this page" when logged out.
- The 12-month proprietary option exists only for members of the "tfopwg" group. "All data that are uploaded without the optional proprietary period will be publicly available immediately."

Our two stars:
- Target pages exist for both TIC 87055304 and TIC 87055315 (target.php?id=...). Today each shows TOIs 0, CTOIs 0, Files 0 and Observing Notes 0.
- A public observing note and files on TIC 87055304 (and on 87055315) saying "4.136-d 0.4% dip is a 2.1% eclipse on 9.3-arcsec neighbour TIC 87055315" is the one ExoFOP channel that needs no published paper. It still needs an approved account.
- "Follow your favorite targets" (add_new.php?param=mytois; login needed) emails updates for chosen targets, which would flag a future TOI on TIC 87055304.

TFOP Working Group (https://tess.mit.edu/followup/ and /followup/apply-join-tfop/):
- SG1 (chair Karen Collins, CfA) does "Seeing-limited Photometry to identify false positives due to nearby eclipsing binaries".
- Observers apply to the subgroup chairs, sending instrument details and 2–3 example light curves for citizen scientists. "General" members without facilities email Dave Latham. Members must agree to the TFOP Charter and Publication Policy.
- SG1 works on TOIs. TIC 87055304 is not a TOI, so there is nothing for SG1 to act on now.
- If QLP alerts it later, a note or files on the TOI page and/or an email to the SG1 chair would be the natural route. That is our interpretation, not a documented submission procedure.

The only object near an existing TOI:
- EB TIC 320327029 (P = 4.4407 d) is 154″ from TOI 3276.01 (TIC 320327056; P = 7.0327 d, TFOPWG PC, "found in faint-star QLP search").
- The periods are not commensurate (ratio 1.58), so this EB cannot be the source of the TOI signal and gives TFOP nothing useful.

What this implies for S103–S105 (projection, not verified):
- SPOC 2-min TOIs: S103 ended 2026-05-17, S104 2026-06-13, S105 2026-07-11. At the usual ~80–120 d delay these would be expected from about mid-Sep to early Nov 2026, so S103 and S104 are already later than the recent pattern.
- QLP faint search for S104 and S105: at the recent 200–420 d delay, roughly Jan–Aug 2027.

What this means for TIC 87055304:
- MAST holds only QLP (S13, 39, 66, 93, 104) and GSFC-eleanor-lite (S13) light curves for it. There are no SPOC 2-min or TESS-SPOC products, so any TOI would have to come from QLP. At T = 11.7 that would be the faint search.
- QLP has already released its S93 faint-search TOIs for this part of the sky, including targets with the same sector set (13, 39, 66, 93). Examples: TOI 7835.01 at 18:01:30 −40:03 and TOI 7913.01 at 18:04:55 −53:54.
- TIC 87055304 was not alerted from S93. Why (no detection, triage, or a centroid flag) is not public and not verified.
- So a QLP alert from S104 is possible but has no precedent so far, and it would most likely come in 2027.

Notifications: the TOI mailing list at http://mailman.mit.edu/mailman/listinfo/tess-toi-info (linked from https://tess.mit.edu/toi-releases/), or ExoFOP's target-follow emails.

other_venues.suits: Individual new EBs: TIC 87055315 (the EBLM-type neighbour), TIC 114787953 and TIC 100666720 (in no catalogue we checked), and the 59 EBs that appear only in Kostov+2025's unvetted list without periods (we add periods and epochs). This is the standard place to record a new variable star. It is not an exoplanet venue.
other_venues.how: Needs an AAVSO/VSX account. Use the New Star form with: a Gaia position, the TIC/Gaia identifiers, type (EA etc.), period, epoch of minimum, magnitude range with passband, and a phase plot (EBs plotted from phase -0.25 to 1.25). Cite TESS (Ricker 2014, 2014SPIE.9143E..20R) and QLP (Huang 2020, 2020RNAAS...4..204H). Limits: 'Only 5 submissions per week are allowed per user' and 'Only 1 submission is allowed for new users until they get one approved.' 'If you are performing a systematic search of variables resulting in lots of new objects, we encourage you to publish those results in a journal (e.g. JAAVSO or PZP) instead'; for bulk uploads, contact the administrators. Data-mined submissions are judged more strictly ('we expect the submitter to do some work, such as period analysis'). The TESS guidance reads 'Useless in most fields due to blending' with a contamination radius of about 120 arcsec, so moderators will want proof of which star varies; our pixel-level localisation of TIC 87055315 is exactly that evidence. Discovery credit is not given 'if the object has already been published'. Whether Kostov+2025's unvetted neural-net list counts as published is unclear (our interpretation; the FAQ treats the spurious-heavy ATLAS catalogue as a special case). No rule on AI or automated analysis was found in the Guidelines or FAQ text (checked 2026-10-12). Note: www.aavso.org returns 403 through our proxy; vsx.aavso.org is reachable.

other_venues.venue: JAAVSO / Peremennye Zvezdy Prilozhenie / OEJV (refereed variable-star journals)
other_venues.suits: A catalogue paper on all 62 EBs: periods, epochs, depths, secondaries, plus the TIC 87055315 blend. VSX itself recommends this route for systematic searches. A refereed paper would also make the objects citable, and would technically let a CTOI-style FP entry go on ExoFOP if wanted.
other_venues.how: Submit a paper. VSX lists OEJV ('Electronic only. Now refereed'), Peremennye Zvezdy ('Refereed'), JAAVSO ('fully refereed... page charge for non-members') and PASP. IBVS stopped accepting submissions on 10 March 2019 and itself recommends JAAVSO, OEJV, PZ, RNAAS and VSX. The current OEJV site (oejv.physics.muni.cz) reset our connection, so its author rules are not verified.

other_venues.suits: A short, quick note, e.g. 'The 4.136-d signal toward TIC 87055304 is an EBLM-type eclipse on TIC 87055315', or a summary of the EB list. On its own this does NOT make a CTOI eligible: ExoFOP accepts an RNAAS only if the detection and vetting methodology was already published in a peer-reviewed journal and is cited.
other_venues.how: Not peer reviewed (an editor checks scope and format). At most 1,500 words and one figure or table; abstract required; no author charges. The AAS AI/LLM guidelines (page says 'initially posted on 9 September 2026') require disclosing AI use, forbid listing AI as an author, and forbid unsupervised LLM generation of any part of the manuscript. Details were obtained via WebFetch because journals.aas.org returns 403 to curl.

other_venues.venue: ExoFOP-TESS observing notes and files on TIC 87055304 / TIC 87055315
other_venues.suits: The 'this future TOI is actually a nearby EB' information, attached where TOI vetters and TFOP SG1 would look if QLP ever alerts TIC 87055304. Needs no published paper.
other_venues.how: An approved ExoFOP account (professional-level work and an affiliation; 'Citizen Scientist' is one of the Position options), then target page > Add new > Observing Notes or Files, with a data tag. Uploads are public immediately. Not tested: we cannot log in.

other_venues.suits: Nearby-EB false-positive information for existing TOIs. TIC 87055304 is not a TOI, so nothing to do now. If it is alerted, SG1 is the group that checks for a nearby EB.
other_venues.how: Membership by application to the subgroup chair (SG1: Karen Collins, kcollins@cfa.harvard.edu) or, for general members, to Dave Latham. Applicants must agree to the TFOP Charter and Publication Policy; citizen scientists send 2–3 example results. Membership gives tfopwg access on ExoFOP.

other_venues.venue: Kostov et al. 2025 'TESS Ten Thousand' catalogue / Eclipsing Binary Patrol (Zooniverse)
other_venues.suits: The 59 EBs that appear only in Kostov+2025's list of about 900,000 unvetted neural-net candidates (score > 0.9, no periods). Our periods and pixel-level vetting are the kind of validation that catalogue's vetted set uses.
other_venues.how: No formal submission route found (not verified). The NASA project page invites volunteers to 'Fill out this form to join the advanced user group and participate in meetings with the science team'; or contact the authors (V. Kostov et al., arXiv:2506.05631).

other_venues.venue: Prša et al. 2022 TESS EB catalogue (Villanova)
other_venues.suits: Checking known EBs, mainly 2-min targets from sectors 1–26. Not a submission venue.
other_venues.how: No submission route found; http://tessebs.villanova.edu/ returned HTTP 400 to curl. Contact the authors if relevant (not verified).

other_venues.suits: Planet-like transit signals spotted by volunteers. Not suitable for EBs. PHT now uploads its CTOIs with an RNAAS citation, e.g. mason's CTOI 392664683.01 on 2026-10-08 citing doi 10.3847/2515-5172/aeaee1, which is a precedent for the RNAAS route.
other_venues.how: Volunteer classification and Talk boards; candidates are written up by the PHT science team.
